title: A Horizon for the Escarpment
premise: Isandro Montrose, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding from her family's debts in a river port town, is the last person to hear from an upriver survey expedition before their radio goes silent. When she realizes their route crosses her late father's sealed escarpment lines—lines he died protecting and she inherited on paper alone—she joins a rival salvage crew racing to reach the wrecked expedition barge. The journey forces her to choose between erasing her father's legacy to save herself or claiming it at the cost of everything she's built in hiding. She reaches the wreck by the fifth tide, exposes the salvage fleet's sabotage of the expedition, and opens the escarpment line as a public passage, finally belonging somewhere by inheriting it honestly.
about_author: Bram Ravensworth is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six seasons mapping glacial rivers before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for technical precision, unforgiving landscapes, and protagonists who negotiate with the past rather than outrun it.

chapters.title: The Last Clear Transmission
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Working radio watch in the port of Vell's Landing, Isandro logs the Halvard expedition's final garbled transmission—a bearing that matches her father's closed escarpment line. She files nothing, tells no one, and lies awake with the compass he left her. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as pragmatism; the debt of silence begins accruing interest.

chapters.title: A Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A salvage fleet broker, Odile Ferran, arrives hunting the expedition's cargo manifest and offers Isandro money for anything she knows about the escarpment routes. Isandro refuses but studies her father's sealed survey folio that night, finding annotations that suggest the line was closed to hide something, not because it failed. Beat: inheritance revealed as both burden and bait.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The harbormaster confirms the calving season will open the upper river gorge for roughly six tides before ice seals it. Ferran's fleet prepares to run the gorge regardless of what happened to the Halvard crew. Isandro, unable to shake the final transmission, signs onto Ferran's lead vessel as navigator—the one job no one else can do. Beat: invisibility ends; she chooses motion over safety.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Aboard the salvage tug Corvane, Isandro navigates the lower rapids while earning the crew's wary respect—and noticing Ferran's charts contain a deliberate error near the second narrows. A deckhand, Teo, catches her comparing charts and becomes her reluctant ally. Beat: trust built in small increments against a backdrop of institutional rot.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Teo. Shifting perspective, Teo reveals the fleet's real contract: not rescue, but recovery of the Halvard's sealed strongbox, and orders to leave survivors unreported. Isandro confronts Ferran, who counters by exposing Isandro's outstanding debts and offering to buy them out—for her father's full folio. Beat: the price of survival made literal; betrayal offered politely.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Bearing
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the second narrows, Isandro secretly corrects the fleet's sabotaged chart, saving the Corvane from a wreck that would have stranded them all—but revealing she knows the water better than anyone aboard. Ferran now understands exactly what Isandro inherited. Beat: competence as exposure; she can no longer pretend to be nobody.

chapters.title: Signal Fire at Kilometer Forty
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Running ahead of the fleet through a side channel on a stolen skiff with Teo, Isandro finds the Halvard's camp: two survivors, half-starved, guarding evidence that Ferran's company bribed the expedition's engineer to falsify the gorge survey. One survivor recognizes her father's name. Beat: grief and fury braided together; the past stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Racing the calving season, Isandro leads the survivors downriver as the glacier begins to groan apart behind them. Ferran's fleet closes in at the gorge mouth, demanding the strongbox and the folio. Isandro broadcasts the survivors' testimony over open radio channels to every port on the network. Beat: climax—she spends her secrecy like currency and buys the truth with it.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. With the glacier failing above, Isandro runs the Corvane itself through the true escarpment line—her father's line—using his annotated bearings while Ferran's other vessels founder on their false charts. The gorge seals behind them in thunder and spray. Ferran is taken into custody at Vell's Landing. Beat: survival achieved not by escaping the past but by navigating straight through it.

chapters.title: Open Passage
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Months later, the escarpment line reopens as a certified public route under Isandro's engineering stamp—her first honest signature since disgrace. She pays her debts from the salvage award, keeps the compass, and hangs her father's folio framed beside her own new surveys. Beat: resolution—belonging earned not by hiding from inheritance but by finishing it.
